chunks: And from him, from Fadala, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Isa ibn Abi Mansur, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When the sun has passed its zenith, and you have prayed its two rak'ahs (subhatah), then the time for Dhuhr has entered.'
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:
I asked him about the time for the prayer of Dhuhr and 'Asr, so he wrote: 'A standing [for Dhuhr] and a standing [for 'Asr].'

key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: The sun has passed its zenith (midday)
key_terms.سُبْحَتَكَ: The two rak'ahs of Dhuhr prayer
key_terms.قَامَةٌ: A standing (referring to the duration or nature of the prayer time)

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Dhuhr prayer begin according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise onset of Dhuhr prayer, defining it as the moment the sun begins its decline from the zenith (zawal), a foundational concept in Shia fiqh for determining prayer times. The reference to 'a standing' (qamata) for both Dhuhr and 'Asr highlights the continuous, uninterrupted nature of these prayers' windows, reflecting the Imam's emphasis on the stability and defined duration of worship periods.
